# Prepare SDD Handoff

## Purpose

Produce the framework-independent Product Handoff for one approved delivery slice and place it
where the SDD workflow consumes it: the handoff document, the generated `product-context.md`, and
the coverage mapping scaffold. The handoff carries exactly the product subgraph the increment
needs, with digests and provenance, and it carries the change's unresolved product questions to
the SDD side. Generation is deterministic tooling; this skill orchestrates and verifies it.

## When to use

- A delivery slice has status `approved`, its change's overlay validates, and a backlog item
  exists for it.
- An existing handoff must be regenerated because its status check reports it stale and the team
  decided to refresh it.

Do not use this skill for unapproved slices (the generator refuses them — PRODUCT040), to create
tracker issues, or to do any SDD-side work (proposal, specs, design, tasks) — SDD owns those.

## Required inputs

- The Product Change ID (`CHG-...`) and the approved slice ID (`SLI-...`).
- The work-item reference in provider form: `<provider>:<owner>/<repo>#<id>`, for example
  `github:acme/shop#123`. The human supplies it; creating tracker issues via API is out of scope
  in v0.1.
- The handoff destination: either an output directory (`--out <dir>`) or the configured SDD
  adapter (for OpenSpec, the name of the native SDD change the sidecars land inside).
- A working `product-definition` CLI.

## Files to read

- `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/change.md` — status, operations and, above all, the
  `## Open Questions` section to be reported to the SDD side.
- `docs/product/changes/active/<chg-id>/slices/<sli-id>.yaml` — status, implements, affects,
  verification, out-of-scope.
- `docs/specification/handoff-contract.md` — the normative handoff contract and closure rule.
- `skills/prepare-sdd-handoff/references/handoff-checklist.md` — pre- and post-generation checks.
- After generation: the generated `product-handoff.yaml` and `product-context.md`.

## Deterministic commands

- `prodshape change validate <CHG-ID>` — the overlay must validate before generating.
- `prodshape handoff create --change <CHG-ID> --slice <SLI-ID>
--work-item <provider:owner/repo#id> [--title <t>] (--out <dir> | --adapter openspec
--sdd-change <name>)` — generate the handoff. With the openspec adapter, the sidecar files
  (`product-handoff.yaml`, `product-context.md`, `product-coverage.yaml`) are placed inside the
  named native SDD change directory.
- `prodshape handoff status <path>` — verify the generated handoff: `current`, `stale`,
  `invalid` or `source-revision-unavailable`.
- `prodshape coverage check <path>` — later in the flow, validates the
  requirement-coverage evidence in an SDD change directory; run it when asked to check coverage,
  not as part of generation.

## Reasoning procedure

1. Read the slice file. Confirm `status: approved` and that `product-change` names the containing
   change. If the slice is not approved, stop and report — do not change its status, do not
   generate.
2. Run `prodshape change validate <CHG-ID>`. If there are errors, stop and report them;
   an invalid overlay has no business feeding an implementation.
3. Confirm the work-item reference. It must be in `<provider>:<owner>/<repo>#<id>` form and refer
   to a backlog item the team already created. If none exists, stop and ask the human to create
   the backlog item and supply the reference — this skill never calls tracker APIs.
4. Work through the pre-flight section of `references/handoff-checklist.md`.
5. Run `prodshape handoff create` with the change, slice, work-item reference and the
   configured destination (adapter or `--out`). Record the command and its output verbatim.
6. Run `prodshape handoff status <path>` on the result. Require `current`. If `invalid`
   or `stale` immediately after generation, something is wrong upstream — stop, report the named
   artifacts and diagnostics, and do not patch the files.
7. Read the generated `product-context.md`. Verify it begins with the generated marker naming the
   handoff ID, that the implemented requirements and their acceptance content are present, and
   that it contains no technical design.
8. Extract the change's unresolved product questions (from `change.md` `## Open Questions`, also
   surfaced in the context) and report them explicitly to the SDD side in your summary — they are
   the questions the implementation must not silently answer.
9. Write the short handoff summary: the handoff ID and location, the slice outcome, the
   implemented requirements (with any partial-coverage scopes), the verification declarations,
   and the open questions. Remind the SDD side of its boundary: report questions and
   contradictions back; never rewrite product knowledge; archiving the SDD change never promotes
   the Product Change.

## Allowed modifications

- Run `prodshape handoff create`, which writes the generated files at the destination.
- Write the handoff summary where the human asks for it (chat, or a file inside the SDD change if
  requested).

## Forbidden actions

- Never generate for a slice that is not `approved`, and never set slice or change status to make
  generation possible.
- Never edit the generated files by hand — `product-handoff.yaml`, `product-context.md` and
  `product-coverage.yaml` are tooling-owned; hand edits break digests and traceability.
- Never modify `docs/product/model` or the change's `proposed/` artifacts.
- Never add technical design, tasks, class names or framework choices to product artifacts or to
  the handoff summary.
- Never create tracker issues through provider APIs; the work-item reference is recorded, not
  automated, in v0.1.
- Never run `prodshape change promote`; archiving or completing SDD work never triggers
  promotion.
- Never answer the change's open questions on the SDD side's behalf; carry them, verbatim.
- Preserve stable IDs everywhere in the SDD workspace: refer to `CHG-`, `SLI-`, `FR-`, `UC-` and
  other artifacts by ID; never paraphrase an ID or copy artifact bodies into SDD documents.

## Human approval points

- Slice approval precedes this skill; verify it, never grant it.
- The human supplies (or confirms) the work-item reference and the SDD destination.
- If the handoff comes out stale or invalid, the human decides between fixing the upstream change
  and regenerating; do not decide unilaterally.
- Promotion, later, is a separate explicit human decision this skill never touches.

## Expected outputs

- A handoff at the destination whose `handoff status` is `current`: `product-handoff.yaml` and
  `product-context.md` (plus `product-coverage.yaml` with the openspec adapter), inside the named
  SDD change when an adapter is used.
- A short summary naming the handoff ID, the slice outcome, the implemented requirements with
  coverage scopes, and every unresolved product question carried to the SDD side.

## Completion checks

- `prodshape change validate <CHG-ID>` exited 0 before generation.
- `prodshape handoff status <path>` reports `current`.
- The generated files exist at the intended destination and were not hand-edited.
- `product-context.md` starts with the generated marker and contains the implemented
  requirements' acceptance content and the change's open questions.
- The summary lists implemented requirements and open questions, and states the SDD boundary.
